source_label: Cocaine - Merck Manual Professional Edition: noradrenergic activity causes the sympathomimetic signs
source_quote: Increased noradrenergic activity accounts for its sympathomimetic effects (tachycardia, hypertension, mydriasis, diaphoresis, vasoconstriction, and hyperthermia).

source_label: Multiple Sclerosis - Merck Manual Professional Edition: relapsing central deficits and periventricular lesions
source_quote: Multiple sclerosis is characterized by varied CNS deficits, with remissions and recurring exacerbations.

source_label: Ischemic Stroke - Merck Manual Professional Edition: infarcts appear as CT hypodensities and CT excludes hemorrhage
source_quote: Within 6 to 12 hours of ischemia, medium-sized to large infarcts start to become visible as hypodensities.

source_label: Choledocholithiasis and Cholangitis - Merck Manual Professional Edition: obstruction causes jaundice before infected cholangitis
source_quote: More complete obstruction causes duct dilation, jaundice and, eventually, ascending cholangitis with bacterial infection.

source_label: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - Merck Manual Professional Edition: insulin resistance with inadequate insulin secretion
source_quote: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is characterized by insulin resistance and inadequate insulin secretion relative to needs.

source_label: Hypertensive Emergencies - Merck Manual Professional Edition: failed autoregulation transmits pressure into capillaries
source_quote: As a result, the very high BP is transmitted directly to the capillary bed with transudation and exudation of plasma into the brain, causing cerebral edema, including papilledema.

source_label: Pulmonary Embolism - Merck Manual Professional Edition: sudden dyspnea and pleuritic pain; oral contraceptives are a risk factor
source_quote: Symptoms of pulmonary embolism are nonspecific and include dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, and, in more severe cases, light-headedness, presyncope, syncope, or cardiorespiratory arrest.

source_label: Alcohol-Related Liver Disease - Merck Manual Professional Edition: AST to ALT ratio at least 2 in alcoholic hepatitis
source_quote: The ratio of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) to alanine aminotransferase (ALT) is ≥ 2.

source_label: Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome - Merck Manual Professional Edition: two of three among hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic morphology
source_quote: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (formerly, polycystic ovary syndrome) is a clinical syndrome defined by the presence 2 of 3 findings: hyperandrogenism (eg, hirsutism, acne), ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovarian morphology.

source_label: Hyperthyroidism - Merck Manual Professional Edition: low thyroglobulin indicates factitious hormone; pretibial myxedema is Graves dermopathy
source_quote: If thyrotoxicosis factitia is suspected, serum thyroglobulin can be measured; it is usually low or low-normal—unlike in all other causes of hyperthyroidism.

source_label: Preeclampsia and Eclampsia - Merck Manual Professional Edition: increased soluble Flt-1 contributes to vasospasm
source_quote: Factors that may contribute to vasospasm include decreased prostacyclin (an endothelium-derived vasodilator), increased endothelin (an endothelium-derived vasoconstrictor), and increased soluble Flt-1 (a circulating receptor for vascular endothelial growth factor).

source_label: Thyroid Disorders in Pregnancy - Merck Manual Professional Edition: propylthiouracil is the usual antithyroid drug in pregnancy
source_quote: Usually, pregnant women are given the lowest possible dose of oral propylthiouracil (50 to 100 mg every 8 hours).

source_label: Beta-Oxidation Cycle Disorders - Merck Manual Professional Edition: MCAD causes hypoketotic hypoglycemia and medium-chain acylcarnitines
source_quote: Diagnosis of MCADD is by detecting medium-chain fatty acid conjugates of carnitine in plasma or glycine in urine or by detecting enzyme deficiency in cultured fibroblasts.

source_label: Rheumatoid Arthritis - Merck Manual Professional Edition: symmetric small-joint synovitis with prolonged morning stiffness
source_quote: Typically, stiffness lasts > 60 minutes after rising in the morning but may occur after any prolonged inactivity (called gelling).

source_label: Evaluation of the Shoulder - Merck Manual Professional Edition: the empty-can test assesses supraspinatus
source_quote: The supraspinatus is assessed by having the patient resist downward pressure on the arms held in flexion (forward) with the thumbs pointing downward and the elbow extended (empty can, or Jobe test).

source_label: Gout - Merck Manual Professional Edition: monosodium urate crystals cause recurrent podagra
source_quote: Gout is a disorder caused by the precipitation of monosodium urate crystals in and around joints, most often causing recurrent acute or chronic arthritis.

source_label: Osteoporosis - Merck Manual Professional Edition: decreased bone mineral density with structural deterioration
source_quote: Osteoporosis is a progressive metabolic bone disease that decreases bone mineral density (bone mass per unit volume), with deterioration of bone structure.

source_label: Lupus Nephritis - Merck Manual Professional Edition: immune-complex deposition causes the glomerulonephritis
source_quote: Pathophysiology involves immune complex deposition with development of glomerulonephritis.

source_label: Spinal Cord Infarction - Merck Manual Professional Edition: anterior spinal artery infarct spares posterior-column sensation
source_quote: Pain and temperature sensation are disproportionately impaired; position and vibration sensation, conducted by the posterior columns, and often light touch are relatively spared.

source_label: Ischemic Stroke - Merck Manual Professional Edition: dominant middle cerebral artery causes face-and-arm weakness plus aphasia
source_quote: Contralateral hemiparesis (worse in the arm and face than in the leg), dysarthria, hemianesthesia, contralateral homonymous hemianopia, aphasia (if the dominant hemisphere is affected) or apraxia and sensory neglect (if the nondominant hemisphere is affected) Middle cerebral artery (common).

source_label: Antiseizure Medications - Merck Manual Professional Edition: oxcarbazepine causes hyponatremia
source_quote: Fatigue, nausea, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, somnolence, leukopenia, diplopia, hyponatremia (in 2.5%).

source_label: Medications for Treatment of Depression - Merck Manual Professional Edition: venlafaxine blocks serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake
source_quote: These medications (eg, desvenlafaxine , duloxetine , levomilnacipran , milnacipran , venlafaxine ) have a dual 5-HT and norepinephrine mechanism of action, as do tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs).

source_label: Drug Eruptions and Reactions - Merck Manual Professional Edition: DRESS is fever, facial edema, rash, eosinophilia, and hepatitis weeks after a drug
source_quote: Manifests as fever, facial edema, and rash 2–6 weeks after first dose of a medication.

source_label: Organophosphate Poisoning and Carbamate Poisoning - Merck Manual Professional Edition: give pralidoxime after atropine
source_quote: Pralidoxime (2-PAM) is given after atropine to relieve neuromuscular symptoms.

source_label: Aspirin and Other Salicylate Poisoning - Merck Manual Professional Edition: respiratory alkalosis plus metabolic acidosis
source_quote: Usually, ABGs or VBGs show primary respiratory alkalosis during the first few hours after ingestion; later, they show compensated metabolic acidosis or mixed metabolic acidosis/respiratory alkalosis.

source_label: Indolent B-Cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma Treatment (PDQ) - NCI: BCL2 overexpression inhibits apoptosis in follicular lymphoma
source_quote: Overexpression of the BCL2 protein is associated with the inability to eradicate the lymphoma by inhibiting apoptosis.

source_label: The opioid-impaired provider - NIH PMC: stop an impaired colleague from practicing and use a physician health program
source_quote: Intervene in a timely manner to ensure that impaired colleagues cease practicing and receive appropriate assistance from a physician health program.

source_label: Celiac Disease - Merck Manual Professional Edition: gluten-driven inflammation causes villous atrophy and malabsorption
source_quote: The inflammatory response causes characteristic mucosal villous atrophy in the small bowel.

source_label: Acute Kidney Injury - Merck Manual Professional Edition: prerenal injury is poor perfusion with low urine sodium
source_quote: Hypoperfusion of an otherwise functioning kidney leads to enhanced reabsorption of sodium and water, resulting in oliguria (urine output < 500 mL/day) with high urine osmolality and low urine sodium.

source_label: Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure - Merck Manual Professional Edition: bilateral opacities and respiratory failure not explained by heart failure
source_quote: Respiratory failure not fully explained by heart failure or fluid overload.

source_label: Acid-Base Disorders - Merck Manual Professional Edition — mixed disorders can leave measured values deceptively normal
source_quote: In these mixed disorders, values may be deceptively normal.

source_label: Preeclampsia and Eclampsia - Merck Manual Professional Edition — severe features are severe hypertension or end-organ injury, and HELLP also requires hemolysis
source_quote: Preeclampsia with severe features is diagnosed in patients with new onset of persistent severe hypertension and/or signs or symptoms of end-organ damage.

source_label: Control of confounding in the analysis phase – an overview for clinicians — a confounder is associated with both the exposure and the outcome
source_quote: Confounding arises when a factor is associated with both the exposure (or treatment) and the outcome, eg, a disease or death, and is not part of the causal pathway from exposure to outcome.

source_label: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia Caused by 21-Hydroxylase Deficiency - Merck Manual Professional Edition — precursors enter androgen synthesis while aldosterone deficiency wastes salt
source_quote: The salt-wasting form of classic 21-hydroxylase deficiency causes hyponatremia (sometimes severe), hyperkalemia, and hypotension as well as virilization.

source_label: Excessive Bleeding - Merck Manual Professional Edition — standard clotting times do not measure factor XIII, and a factor XIII-deficient clot lyses in urea
source_quote: The aPTT tests for deficiencies of all clotting factors except factor VII (measured by the PT) and factor XIII (measured by a factor XIII assay).

source_label: Understanding Medical Tests and Test Results - Merck Manual Professional Edition — a confirmatory cutoff favors specificity over sensitivity
source_quote: If a test is designed to confirm a disease, a cutoff point with greater specificity and lower sensitivity is selected.

source_label: Hyponatremia - Merck Manual Professional Edition — low effective circulating volume in heart failure releases vasopressin
source_quote: In each of these disorders, a decrease in effective circulating volume results in the release of vasopressin and angiotensin II.

source_label: Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies - Merck Manual Professional Edition — dermatomyositis is a small-vessel vasculopathy with perifascicular inflammation
source_quote: Dermatomyositis is characterized by immune complex deposition in the vessels and is considered a complement-mediated vasculopathy.

source_label: Hyponatremia - Merck Manual Professional Edition — inappropriate antidiuretic hormone leaves the urine less than maximally dilute despite low plasma osmolality
source_quote: The syndrome of inappropriate ADH ( vasopressin ) secretion is attributed to excessive vasopressin release.

source_label: Gout - Merck Manual Professional Edition — allopurinol decreases azathioprine metabolism and potentiates marrow toxicity
source_quote: Allopurinol is contraindicated in patients taking azathioprine or mercaptopurine because it can decrease metabolism of these medications and thus potentiate their immunosuppressive and cytolytic effects.

source_label: Male Reproductive Endocrinology - Merck Manual Professional Edition — inhibin B inhibits FSH, whereas estradiol is the main inhibitor of LH
source_quote: In males, estradiol is the main inhibitor of LH production, whereas both estradiol and inhibin B, a peptide produced by Sertoli cells of the testes, inhibit production of FSH.

source_label: Bioethics for clinicians: 23. Disclosure of medical error — tell the patient what happened, the consequences, and the plan to prevent recurrence
source_quote: Disclose promptly what you know about the event.

source_label: Acute Kidney Injury - Merck Manual Professional Edition — NSAIDs reduce renal perfusion by afferent arteriolar constriction, and volume depletion is a prerenal state
source_quote: Medications that reduce renal perfusion (eg, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors or angiotensin II receptor blockers, calcineurin inhibitors).

source_label: Tremor - Merck Manual Professional Edition — intention tremor increases as the limb reaches its target, while a resting tremor lessens with activity
source_quote: Intention tremors have a crescendo and increase as the affected body part reaches its target.

source_label: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease - Merck Manual Professional Edition — loss of radial airway traction in emphysema lets airways collapse
source_quote: Emphysema is destruction of lung parenchyma leading to a loss of elastic recoil, loss of alveolar septa, and radial airway traction, which increases the tendency for airway collapse.

source_label: Guillain-Barré Syndrome - Merck Manual Professional Edition — cerebrospinal fluid can show high protein with a normal white-cell count
source_quote: CSF analysis may detect albuminocytologic dissociation (increased protein but normal white blood cell count), but it may not appear for up to 1 week and does not develop in 10% of patients.

source_label: Rheumatoid Arthritis - Merck Manual Professional Edition — inflammatory stiffness lasts more than 60 minutes after rising
source_quote: Typically, stiffness lasts > 60 minutes after rising in the morning but may occur after any prolonged inactivity (called gelling).

source_label: Aortic Dissection - Merck Manual Professional Edition — blood enters through an intimal tear and splits the media
source_quote: Aortic dissection is the surging of blood through a tear in the aortic intima with separation of the intima and media and creation of a false lumen (channel).

source_label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus - Merck Manual Professional Edition — anti-dsDNA antibody is highly specific for systemic lupus erythematosus
source_quote: Positive ANA should prompt more specific testing such as anti-dsDNA antibodies; anti-dsDNA is highly specific for SLE.

source_label: Lupus Nephritis - Merck Manual Professional Edition — low complement and anti-dsDNA antibody indicate active lupus nephritis
source_quote: Elevated anti-dsDNA antibody titers and low complement levels often indicate active lupus nephritis and support the diagnosis.

source_label: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia - Merck Manual Professional Edition — BCR-ABL fusion kinase drives the disease, and the smear shows immature granulocytes and basophilia
source_quote: The chimeric fusion gene BCR::ABL is responsible for production of the oncoprotein BCR::ABL tyrosine kinase.

source_label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus - Merck Manual Professional Edition — anti-dsDNA antibody marks lupus, and drug-induced lupus follows other medicines
source_quote: Positive ANA should prompt more specific testing such as anti-dsDNA antibodies; anti-dsDNA is highly specific for SLE.

source_label: Metabolic Dysfunction–Associated Steatotic Liver Disease - Merck Manual Professional Edition — steatosis with a metabolic risk factor and little or no alcohol, with AST/ALT usually below 1
source_quote: Metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD, previously known as fatty liver or nonalcoholic fatty liver disease [NAFLD]) is defined as the presence of hepatic steatosis in individuals with at least one metabolic risk factor (eg, obesity, dyslipidemia) and minimal or no alcohol consumption

source_label: Alcohol-Related Liver Disease - Merck Manual Professional Edition — moderate alcoholic hepatitis causes fever, jaundice, and tender hepatomegaly, with AST/ALT at least 2
source_quote: Most patients with moderate disease are undernourished and present with fatigue, fever, jaundice, right upper quadrant pain, tender hepatomegaly, and sometimes a hepatic bruit.

source_label: Wheezing - Merck Manual Professional Edition — albuterol is a short-acting beta-2 agonist bronchodilator
source_quote: Wheezing itself can be relieved with inhaled short acting beta2-agonist bronchodilators (eg, albuterol 2.5 mg nebulized solution or 108 mcg metered dose inhalation).

source_label: Atrial Flutter - Merck Manual Professional Edition — 2-to-1 conduction gives a regular ventricular rate near 150 with sawtooth flutter waves
source_quote: Because the atrioventricular (AV) node cannot usually conduct at this rate, typically half of the impulses get through (2:1 block), resulting in a regular ventricular rate of 150 beats/minute.

source_label: Acute Heart Failure - Merck Manual Professional Edition — intravenous loop diuretics are the mainstay of decongestion
source_quote: The mainstay of the pharmacologic management of acute heart failure is decongestive therapy with diuretics, namely loop diuretics (eg, furosemide, torsemide, bumetanide) in either oral or intravenous form.

source_label: Measles - Merck Manual Professional Edition — fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, and a rash that spreads cephalocaudally
source_quote: It is characterized by fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, a characteristic enanthem (Koplik spots) on the oral mucosa, and a maculopapular exanthem that spreads cephalocaudally.

source_label: Pleural Effusion - Merck Manual Professional Edition — dullness, decreased breath sounds, and blunting of the costophrenic angle
source_quote: Physical examination may reveal decreased breath sounds on the side of the effusion, dullness to percussion, and absent tactile fremitus.

source_label: Treatment of Acute COPD Exacerbation - Merck Manual Professional Edition — systemic glucocorticoids are started for exacerbations that are not mild; antibiotics require purulent sputum or ventilatory support
source_quote: Systemic glucocorticoids should be initiated immediately for all but mild exacerbations.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: exacerbation treatment is bronchodilators, glucocorticoids, and oxygen when needed
source_quote: Treatment is with bronchodilators, glucocorticoids, and, when necessary, oxygen and antibiotics.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Acute Complications of Diabetes: DKA is hyperglycemia, hyperketonemia, and metabolic acidosis, often with fruity breath
source_quote: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is an acute metabolic complication of diabetes characterized by hyperglycemia, hyperketonemia, and metabolic acidosis.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Hypothyroidism: medications must be given cautiously because they are metabolized more slowly
source_quote: Finally, all medications should be given cautiously because they are metabolized more slowly than in healthy people.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Confidentiality and HIPAA: communication should follow patient preferences, and information is not shared with family when the patient objects
source_quote: Health care professionals should take reasonable steps to ensure that their communications with the patient are confidential and in accord with patient preferences.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Acute Cholecystitis: right-upper-quadrant pain, tenderness, and fever, with normal or slightly elevated liver tests when uncomplicated
source_quote: In uncomplicated acute cholecystitis, liver tests are normal or only slightly elevated.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Tonsillopharyngitis: penicillin is preferred for group A streptococcus and amoxicillin is also effective; macrolides are for penicillin allergy
source_quote: Amoxicillin is also effective and more palatable if a liquid preparation is required.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Acute Heart Failure: the mainstay of initial drug treatment is a loop diuretic for congestion
source_quote: The mainstay of the pharmacologic management of acute heart failure is decongestive therapy with diuretics, namely loop diuretics (eg, furosemide , torsemide , bumetanide ) in either oral or intravenous form.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Confidentiality and HIPAA: protected health information is not used for purposes unrelated to health care
source_quote: In most situations, PHI may not be used for purposes unrelated to health care.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Confidentiality and HIPAA: disclosures should follow the patient's preferences
source_quote: Health care professionals should take reasonable steps to ensure that their communications with the patient are confidential and in accord with patient preferences.

source_label: NIH PMC, impaired-provider scenario: recognize impairment, remove the colleague from clinical care, and notify the supervising contact
source_quote: This simulation scenario is intended to provide an opportunity for learners to recognize an impaired colleague in a clinical setting, remove them from the clinical care environment, and notify the appropriate contacts, such as a Program Director, Department Chair, or nursing supervisor.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Child Maltreatment: physicians must report suspected child abuse or neglect
source_quote: In the United States, physicians and other professionals in contact with children (eg, nurses, physician assistants, nurse practitioners, social workers, psychologists, teachers, day care workers, police) are mandated reporters who are required by law in every state to report incidents of suspected child abuse or neglect (see Mandatory Reporters of Child Abuse and Neglect ).

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Burns: large burns require fluid resuscitation with lactated Ringer solution
source_quote: Patients with large burns ( > 20% TBSA) require fluid resuscitation.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Brief Psychotic Disorder: psychotic symptoms for days to a month may need supervision and short-term antipsychotic treatment
source_quote: Treatment of brief psychotic disorder is similar to treatment of an acute exacerbation of schizophrenia ; supervision and short-term treatment with antipsychotics may be required.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Ischemic Stroke: alteplase may be given within 3 hours of last known well when contraindications, including hemorrhage on CT, are absent
source_quote: Recombinant tPA ( alteplase ) can be used for patients with acute ischemic stroke up to 3 hours after symptom onset if they have no contraindications to tPA (see table Exclusion Criteria for Use of Tissue Plasminogen Activator in Stroke ).

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Diabetic Ketoacidosis: intravenous regular insulin is given when potassium is at least 3.3 mEq/L, after volume replacement
source_quote: Then, whether or not a bolus has been given, adults should be administered a continuous IV infusion of regular insulin 0.1 unit/kg/hour in 0.9% saline solution.

source_label: MedlinePlus, Uterine fibroids: heavy menstrual bleeding, and a pelvic exam may show a change in the shape and size of the uterus
source_quote: This may show that you have a change in the shape and size of your womb.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Acute Pancreatitis: diagnosis requires compatible pain plus lipase more than three times the upper limit of normal
source_quote: Serum amylase and/or lipase > 3 times the upper limit of normal (normal range of amylase and lipase levels can differ depending on the assay used)

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Intestinal Obstruction: suspected bowel ischemia is treated with resuscitation and operative exploration
source_quote: If bowel ischemia or infarction is suspected, antibiotics should be given (eg, a third-generation cephalosporin, such as cefotetan or cefoxitin ) before operative exploration.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Ventilatory Failure: drugs that suppress ventilatory drive cause hypercapnic respiratory failure, as do severe COPD exacerbations
source_quote: Common causes are severe acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), overdoses of drugs that suppress ventilatory drive, and conditions that cause respiratory muscle weakness (eg, Guillain-Barré syndrome, myasthenia gravis, botulism).

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Acute Coronary Syndromes: unstable angina and NSTEMI together are non-ST-elevation ACS
source_quote: Unstable angina and NSTEMI are also collectively referred to as non-ST elevation ACS (NSTE-ACS).

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Tetralogy of Fallot: toddlers squat during play, and a harsh systolic ejection murmur is heard at the left upper sternal border
source_quote: During play, some toddlers may intermittently squat, a position that increases systemic vascular resistance and aortic pressure, which decreases right-to-left ventricular shunting and thus raises arterial oxygen saturation.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Acute Heart Failure: loop diuretics are the initial decongestive therapy
source_quote: The mainstay of the pharmacologic management of acute heart failure is decongestive therapy with diuretics, namely loop diuretics (eg, furosemide , torsemide , bumetanide ) in either oral or intravenous form.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Pulmonary Embolism: systemic thrombolysis is given for hemodynamic compromise when contraindications are absent
source_quote: Experts agree that systemic thrombolytic therapy should be given to patients with hemodynamic compromise if there are no contraindications, particularly when other means of rapidly reducing clot burden are not readily available.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Ventilatory Failure: noninvasive ventilation is the preferred initial treatment for acute-on-chronic respiratory failure from COPD
source_quote: NIPPV is the preferred initial treatment for many patients with ACRF, resulting in decreased rates of ventilator-associated pneumonia , length of stay, and mortality compared with endotracheal intubation .

source_label: MedlinePlus, Advance Directives: these documents state end-of-life choices, including refusal of resuscitation and breathing machines, for clinicians and family
source_quote: Advance directives are legal documents that allow you to spell out your decisions about end-of-life care ahead of time.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Bronchiolitis: high-risk infants are hospitalized, and care is supportive oxygen and hydration rather than routine corticosteroids or antibiotics
source_quote: Patients who are at risk of developing severe disease should be hospitalized.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Membranous Nephropathy: PLA2R is the major antigen, and the disease is a common cause of nephrotic syndrome in adults
source_quote: Membranous nephropathy mostly affects adults, in whom it is a common cause of nephrotic syndrome ( 1 ).

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Chronic Kidney Disease: SGLT2 inhibitors slow proteinuric CKD with or without diabetes, and combined ACE inhibitor plus ARB therapy is not recommended
source_quote: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors delay progression of proteinuric CKD in patients with or without diabetes, although these medications are contraindicated in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus ( 3 ).

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Community-Acquired Pneumonia: treatment is empiric antibiotics, and hypoxemia is treated with oxygen
source_quote: Supportive care includes fluids, antipyretics (as needed for high-grade fever), analgesics, and, for patients with hypoxemia, oxygen.

source_label: Merck Manual Professional, Tuberculosis: night sweats are classic, pleural effusion causes dyspnea, and HIV is the major predisposing infection
source_quote: Dyspnea may result from lung parenchymal damage, spontaneous pneumothorax, or pleural TB with effusion.

source_label: Pneumocystis jirovecii Pneumonia, Merck Manual Professional Edition: first-line treatment is trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
source_quote: The first-line treatment of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia is with sulfamethoxazole/ trimethoprim (TMP/SMX) ( 1 ).

source_label: Medications for Hypertension, Merck Manual Professional Edition: a limited creatinine rise on an ACE inhibitor is usually tolerated
source_quote: Patients who have stage 3 nephropathy (estimated GFR of < 60 mL/minute to > 30 mL/minute) and are given ACE inhibitors can usually tolerate an increase in serum creatinine up to 30 to 35% above baseline.

source_label: Atrial Fibrillation, Merck Manual Professional Edition: hemodynamic compromise calls for restoration of sinus rhythm
source_quote: In patients with heart failure or other hemodynamic compromise directly attributable to new-onset atrial fibrillation, restoration of normal sinus rhythm is indicated to improve cardiac output ( 1 ).

source_label: Diagnosis of Celiac Disease, NIDDK: do not start a gluten-free diet before diagnostic testing
source_quote: Doctors don’t recommend starting a gluten-free diet before diagnostic testing because a gluten-free diet can affect test results.

source_label: Consent and Surrogate Decision Making, Merck Manual Professional Edition: presumed consent when no surrogate is available
source_quote: When immediate decisions are medically required, the patient is incapacitated , and an authorized surrogate is not immediately available, the doctrine of presumed consent applies.

source_label: Behavior That Undermines a Culture of Safety, ACOG: confidential reporting systems should be established for physicians whose behavior threatens safety
source_quote: Confidential reporting systems and assistance programs for physicians who exhibit disruptive behavior should be established.

source_label: Suicidal Behavior, Merck Manual Professional Edition: imminently suicidal patients stay in a secure setting
source_quote: At-risk patients should not be left alone until they are in a secure environment (often a psychiatric facility or emergency department).

source_label: Parkinson Disease, Merck Manual Professional Edition: levodopa is most effective for bradykinesia and rigidity
source_quote: Levodopa is most effective at relieving bradykinesia and rigidity and often substantially reduces tremor ( 2 ).

source_label: Pneumothorax, Merck Manual Professional Edition: tube thoracostomy for secondary pneumothorax
source_quote: Tube thoracostomy for secondary and traumatic pneumothoraces

source_label: Chronic Kidney Disease, Merck Manual Professional Edition: biopsy is not recommended for small fibrotic kidneys
source_quote: The definitive diagnostic tool is renal biopsy , but it is not recommended when ultrasound indicates small, fibrotic kidneys; high procedural risk outweighs low diagnostic yield.

source_label: Gout, Merck Manual Professional Edition: glucocorticoids treat acute flares; NSAIDs can raise creatinine when renal disease is present
source_quote: Glucocorticoids are used to treat acute flares.

source_label: Crohn Disease, Merck Manual Professional Edition: perianal fistulas are started on a TNF inhibitor, with antibiotics added
source_quote: Patients who have perianal fistulas are treated initially with a TNF inhibitor (eg, infliximab or adalimumab ) ( 1 ).

source_label: Complications of Acute Coronary Syndromes, Merck Manual Professional Edition: aspirin or an NSAID relieves postinfarction pericarditis
source_quote: Aspirin or another nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) usually relieves symptoms.

source_label: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms, Merck Manual Professional Edition: repair above 5.5 cm in a man at acceptable operative risk
source_quote: When the aneurysm becomes > 5 cm in a female or > 5.5 cm in a male and if risk of perioperative complications is lower than estimated risk of rupture, AAA repair is indicated ( 1 ).

source_label: Postpartum Hemorrhage, Merck Manual Professional Edition: massage and oxytocin for uterine atony
source_quote: Hemostasis is attempted by bimanual uterine massage and IV oxytocin infusion.

source_label: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation, Merck Manual Professional Edition: treat the cause and replace consumed factors when bleeding
source_quote: Treatment includes correction of the cause and replacement of platelets, coagulation factors (in fresh frozen plasma), and fibrinogen (in cryoprecipitate) to control severe bleeding.

source_label: Umbilical Cord Prolapse, Merck Manual Professional Edition: variable decelerations suggest cord compression, and position change may relieve it
source_quote: Changing the woman’s position may relieve pressure on the cord; however, if the abnormal fetal heart rate pattern persists, immediate cesarean delivery is necessary.

source_label: Perioperative Management, Merck Manual Professional Edition: do not routinely bridge low-to-moderate thromboembolic risk
source_quote: Routine bridging therapy with heparin is not recommended for patients undergoing surgery who are at low‐to‐moderate risk of thromboembolism.

source_label: Stuttering, NIDCD: most children outgrow stuttering; evaluate after 3 to 6 months or if the child struggles
source_quote: Most children outgrow stuttering.

source_label: Ischemic Stroke, Merck Manual Professional Edition: do not lower blood pressure in acute ischemic stroke except above 220/120 or for reperfusion therapy
source_quote: Perfusion of an ischemic brain area may require an elevated blood pressure (BP) because autoregulation is lost; thus, BP should not be decreased except in the following cases:

source_label: General Principles of Poisoning, Merck Manual Professional Edition: anticholinergic toxidrome is dry skin, mydriasis, and ileus; physostigmine is the antidote
source_quote: Tachycardia, hyperthermia, mydriasis, warm and dry skin, urinary retention, ileus, delirium

source_label: Overview of Abdominal Trauma, Merck Manual Professional Edition: hemodynamic instability from abdominal trauma goes to laparotomy rather than more testing
source_quote: a few patients require exploratory laparotomy rather than testing, including those with: Peritonitis Hemodynamic instability due to abdominal trauma

source_label: Streptococcal Infections, Merck Manual Professional Edition: scarlet fever follows pharyngeal streptococcal infection and has a sandpaper rash
source_quote: Scarlet fever (sometimes called scarlatina), a predominantly childhood disease, usually follows a pharyngeal streptococcal infection; less commonly, it follows streptococcal infections at other sites (eg, the skin).

source_label: Bacterial Meningitis in Infants Over 3 Months of Age, Merck Manual Professional Edition: lumbar puncture when meningitis is suspected, plus empiric antibiotics
source_quote: In general, lumbar puncture should be performed whenever the diagnosis of meningitis is known or suspected in an infant.

source_label: Diphtheria-Tetanus-Pertussis Vaccine, Merck Manual Professional Edition: DTaP at 2, 4, and 6 months
source_quote: The DTaP vaccine is administered as a 5-dose primary series during childhood as follows: at age 2 months, 4 months, 6 months, 15 to 18 months, and 4 to 6 years (before school entry).

source_label: Fever in Infants and Children, Merck Manual Professional Edition: ill-appearing infants 1 to 3 months get lumbar puncture and empiric parenteral antibiotics
source_quote: These infants should be given age-specific empiric parenteral antibiotic therapy (eg, ceftriaxone ) until serious bacterial infection is ruled out by negative cultures or a specific diagnosis is made.

source_label: Hypothyroidism, Merck Manual Professional Edition: levothyroxine is preferred replacement
source_quote: Levothyroxine is preferred; the usual maintenance dose is 75 to 150 mcg orally once a day, depending on age, body mass index, and absorption (for pediatric treatment, see Hypothyroidism in Infants and Children ).

source_label: Hypothyroidism, Merck Manual Professional Edition: primary disease raises TSH and lowers free T4; central disease lowers both
source_quote: serum TSH is always elevated, whereas serum free T4 is low.

source_label: Preventing Type 2 Diabetes, NIDDK: reduced-calorie eating and physical activity delay progression; fasting glucose 100 to 125 mg/dL is prediabetes
source_quote: You can help prevent or delay type 2 diabetes by losing a modest amount of weight by following a reduced-calorie eating plan and being physically active most days of the week.

source_label: Breast Masses, Merck Manual Professional Edition: ultrasound is the usual first test to separate a cyst from a solid mass
source_quote: Typically, this is determined with breast ultrasound ( 1 ).

source_label: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) - Merck Manual Professional Edition: brown granular casts indicate renal tubular injury
source_quote: With renal tubular injury, the sediment characteristically contains tubular cells, tubular cell casts, and many granular casts (often with brown pigmentation).

source_label: Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Merck Manual Professional Edition: lumbar puncture if CT does not show the bleed
source_quote: If subarachnoid hemorrhage is suspected clinically but not identified by neuroimaging, or if neuroimaging is not immediately available, lumbar puncture is performed.

source_label: Postoperative Care - Merck Manual Professional Edition: encourage incentive spirometry after surgery
source_quote: Incentive spirometry and periodic coughing can help decrease risk of pneumonia and should be encouraged up to 10 times once every hour.

source_label: Acute Complications of Diabetes Mellitus - Merck Manual Professional Edition: saline and insulin for diabetic ketoacidosis
source_quote: The most urgent goals for treating diabetic ketoacidosis are rapid intravascular volume repletion, correction of hyperglycemia and acidosis, and prevention of hypokalemia ( 1 , 2 , 3 ).

source_label: Hypertensive Emergencies - Merck Manual Professional Edition: severe hypertension plus target-organ damage
source_quote: A hypertensive emergency is severe hypertension (often defined as systolic blood pressure (BP) ≥ 180 mm Hg and/or diastolic blood pressure ≥ 120 mm Hg) with signs of damage to target organs (primarily the brain, cardiovascular system, and kidneys).

source_label: Ischemic Stroke - Merck Manual Professional Edition: alteplase within 3 hours if no contraindication
source_quote: Recombinant tPA ( alteplase ) can be used for patients with acute ischemic stroke up to 3 hours after symptom onset if they have no contraindications to tPA

source_label: Overview of Diabetes Mellitus - Merck Manual Professional Edition: type 2 diabetes is insulin resistance with relative insulin deficiency
source_quote: Type 1 diabetes is primarily characterized by inadequate insulin production due to autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, whereas type 2 diabetes is primarily characterized by insulin resistance and a relative insufficiency of insulin.

source_label: Sepsis and Septic Shock - Merck Manual Professional Edition: early fluids and antibiotics
source_quote: Because sepsis may progress rapidly, management requires early identification, aggressive fluid resuscitation, antibiotics, and source control.

source_label: Hyperkalemia - Merck Manual Professional Edition: calcium plus insulin and glucose for QRS widening
source_quote: If ECG changes include the loss of P-wave or widening of the QRS complex, treatment with IV calcium as well as insulin and glucose is indicated

source_label: Ischemic Stroke - Merck Manual Professional Edition: CT excludes hemorrhage and confirms the infarct
source_quote: Diagnosis is clinical, but CT or MRI is performed to exclude hemorrhage and confirm the presence and extent of stroke.

source_label: Acute Cholecystitis - Merck Manual Professional Edition: wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid means acute inflammation
source_quote: Pericholecystic fluid or thickening of the gallbladder wall indicates acute inflammation.

source_label: Laparoscopic gallbladder removal - MedlinePlus: common bile duct injury is a risk of the operation
source_quote: Risks for gallbladder surgery include: Damage to the blood vessels that go to the liver Injury to the common bile duct Injury to the small intestine or colon Inflammation of the pancreas (pancreatitis)

source_label: Acute Complications of Diabetes Mellitus - Merck Manual Professional Edition: HHS has very high glucose and osmolality without ketoacidosis
source_quote: This causes more severe dehydration before presentation, and thus plasma glucose ( > 600 mg/dL [ > 33.3 mmol/L]) and osmolality ( > 320 mOsm/L) are typically much higher than in diabetic ketoacidosis.

source_label: Treatment of Acute COPD Exacerbation - Merck Manual Professional Edition: oxygen, bronchodilators, and glucocorticoids together
source_quote: Beta-agonists and anticholinergics, with or without glucocorticoids, should be started concurrently with oxygen therapy (regardless of how oxygen is administered) with the aim of reversing airway obstruction ( 1 ).

source_label: Treatment of Acute Asthma Exacerbations - Merck Manual Professional Edition: inhaled albuterol is the initial reliever
source_quote: Patients having an asthma exacerbation are instructed to self-administer 2 to 4 puffs of inhaled albuterol or a similar short-acting beta agonist up to 3 times spaced 20 minutes apart for an acute exacerbation and to measure peak expiratory flow (PEF) if possible.

source_label: Acute Myocardial Infarction - Merck Manual Professional Edition: ST elevation in II, III, and aVF is inferior infarction
source_quote: There is hyperacute ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF and reciprocal depression in other leads.

source_label: Treatment of Acute COPD Exacerbation - Merck Manual Professional Edition: systemic glucocorticoids for exacerbations that are not mild, with a short-acting beta agonist
source_quote: Systemic glucocorticoids should be initiated immediately for all but mild exacerbations.

source_label: Acute Heart Failure - Merck Manual Professional Edition: loop diuretics are the mainstay of decongestion
source_quote: The mainstay of the pharmacologic management of acute heart failure is decongestive therapy with diuretics, namely loop diuretics (eg, furosemide, torsemide, bumetanide) in either oral or intravenous form.

source_label: Treatment of Acute Asthma Exacerbations - Merck Manual Professional Edition: oxygen to keep saturation above 90%, plus inhaled bronchodilators and a glucocorticoid
source_quote: Supplemental oxygen is indicated for hypoxemia and should be given by nasal cannula or face mask at a flow rate or concentration sufficient to maintain oxygen saturation > 90%.

source_label: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - Merck Manual Professional Edition: insulin resistance with inadequate insulin secretion
source_quote: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is characterized by insulin resistance and inadequate insulin secretion relative to needs.

source_label: Treatment of Acute COPD Exacerbation - Merck Manual Professional Edition: antibiotics for increased dyspnea, sputum volume, and purulence
source_quote: Antibiotics should be initiated if any of the following conditions are met: Presence of three cardinal symptoms: Increase in dyspnea, increase in sputum volume, and increase in sputum purulence.

source_label: Hashimoto Thyroiditis - Merck Manual Professional Edition: diagnosis by high-titer thyroid peroxidase antibodies
source_quote: Diagnosis involves demonstration of high titers of thyroid peroxidase antibodies.

source_label: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease - Merck Manual Professional Edition: an exacerbation is a sporadic increase in symptom severity
source_quote: Acute exacerbations occur sporadically during the course of COPD and are heralded by increased symptom severity.

source_label: Chronic Kidney Disease - Merck Manual Professional Edition: the anemia is usually from deficient erythropoietin
source_quote: It is usually caused by deficient erythropoietin production due to a reduction of functional renal mass (see page Anemias Caused by Deficient Erythropoiesis ).

source_label: Immunize.org Ask the Experts. A mild acute illness with or without fever is not a precaution, and vaccines may be given.
source_quote: A mild acute illness (e.g., diarrhea or mild upper-respiratory tract infection) with or without fever is not a precaution, and vaccines may be given.

source_label: Management of Normal Labor - Merck Manual Professional Edition: the latent phase precedes the active phase and includes dilation to 4 to 6 cm
source_quote: The latent phase is the interval from the onset of labor to the onset of the active phase ( 1 ).

source_label: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - Merck Manual Professional Edition: start insulin for catabolism or for symptomatic hyperglycemia at this glucose and A1c
source_quote: Insulin should generally be considered in patients with evidence of ongoing catabolism (unintentional weight loss) or symptoms of hyperglycemia (ie, polyuria, polydipsia) with HbA1C levels > 10% (86 mmol/mol) and blood glucose levels ≥ 300 mg/dL (16.7 mmol/L) ( 10 ).

source_label: Community-Acquired Pneumonia - Merck Manual Professional Edition: without MRSA or Pseudomonas risk factors, use a beta-lactam plus a macrolide
source_quote: Risk factors for MRSA or Pseudomonas aeruginosa include prior respiratory isolation of MRSA or P. aeruginosa or recent hospitalization + receipt of parenteral antibiotics (in the last 90 days).

source_label: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease - Merck Manual Professional Edition: exacerbations are heralded by increased symptom severity
source_quote: Acute exacerbations occur sporadically during the course of COPD and are heralded by increased symptom severity.

source_label: Treatment of Acute Asthma Exacerbations - Merck Manual Professional Edition: oxygen for saturation at or below 90% and immediate inhaled albuterol
source_quote: Supplemental oxygen is indicated for hypoxemia and should be given by nasal cannula or face mask at a flow rate or concentration sufficient to maintain oxygen saturation > 90%.

source_label: PMC review of acute asthma: a normal PaCO2 during a severe attack signals impending respiratory fatigue and is listed with life-threatening asthma.
source_quote: A normal partial pressure of CO 2 (PaCO 2 )in a patient with a severe asthma attack can be a sign of impending respiratory fatigue.

source_label: ATS/IDSA community-acquired pneumonia guideline: start empiric antibiotics regardless of the initial procalcitonin.
source_quote: We recommend that empiric antibiotic therapy should be initiated in adults with clinically suspected and radiographically confirmed CAP regardless of initial serum procalcitonin level (strong recommendation, moderate quality of evidence).

source_label: Merck Manual, Approach to the Trauma Patient: uncertain airway protection or oxygenation requires endotracheal intubation, and a neck hematoma can threaten the airway.
source_quote: Obtunded patients whose airway patency, airway protective mechanisms, oxygenation, or ventilation is uncertain and patients with significant oropharyngeal injury require endotracheal intubation

source_label: MedlinePlus, Iron deficiency anemia: iron supplements rebuild stores, and colonoscopy and upper endoscopy are used to look for blood loss.
source_quote: To check for causes of blood loss, your provider may order: Colonoscopy Fecal occult blood test Upper endoscopy

source_label: Merck Manual, drug treatment of diabetes: insulin is required in type 1 diabetes because these patients develop ketoacidosis without it.
source_quote: Insulin is required for all patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus because they do not produce adequate insulin (due to destruction of the pancreatic beta-cells) and will develop ketoacidosis without it.

source_label: Merck Manual, diabetic ketoacidosis: SGLT2 inhibitors can cause euglycemic ketoacidosis, and dextrose is added to insulin therapy when glucose is already low.
source_quote: In pregnant patients and in patients taking SGLT2 inhibitors, DKA may occur at lower or even normal blood glucose levels (euglycemic DKA).

source_label: Merck Manual Professional. Basal insulin suppresses hepatic glucose production, especially in the fasting state.
source_quote: is used to simulate basal insulin production that suppresses hepatic glucose production, especially in the fasting state

source_label: Merck Manual, specific poisons: lithium toxicity is treated with hydration, and dialysis is for a level above 4 mEq/L, end-organ damage, or severe symptoms.
source_quote: Acute: Hydration, diazepam , possibly dialysis for end-organ damage or serum lithium level > 4 mEq/L (4 mmol/L)

source_label: Merck Manual, Hyperthyroidism: the syndrome is hypermetabolism with elevated free thyroid hormone, and TSH is suppressed.
source_quote: Hyperthyroidism is characterized by hypermetabolism and elevated serum levels of free thyroid hormones.

source_label: Merck Manual, Ischemic Stroke: emboli may originate as cardiac thrombi, especially in atrial fibrillation.
source_quote: Emboli may originate as cardiac thrombi, especially in the following conditions: Atrial fibrillation

source_label: Merck Manual, Generalized Anxiety Disorder: treatment is psychotherapy, an SSRI or SNRI, or both, and sustained benzodiazepine use can cause dependence.
source_quote: Treatment includes behavioral interventions, psychotherapy, pharmacotherapy, or a combination.

source_label: Merck Manual, Hyperkalemia: intravenous calcium antagonizes the cardiac effect and is a temporizing measure while other treatment or dialysis is arranged.
source_quote: Calcium infusion is a temporizing measure while awaiting the effects of other treatments or initiation of hemodialysis and may need to be repeated.

source_label: Merck Manual, fetal monitoring: an abnormal pattern, including absent variability with recurrent late decelerations, requires oxygen, repositioning, stopping oxytocin, or preparation for expedited delivery.
source_quote: Abnormal patterns require prompt actions to correct them (eg, supplemental oxygen, repositioning, treatment of maternal hypotension, discontinuation of oxytocin ) or preparation for an expedited delivery.

source_label: Merck Manual, Heart Failure: acute congestion is treated with a loop diuretic such as furosemide, given orally or intravenously.
source_quote: The mainstay of the pharmacologic management of acute heart failure is decongestive therapy with diuretics, namely loop diuretics (eg, furosemide , torsemide , bumetanide ) in either oral or intravenous form.

source_label: Merck Manual, Heart Failure: loop diuretics are the decongestive treatment for acute heart failure.
source_quote: The mainstay of the pharmacologic management of acute heart failure is decongestive therapy with diuretics, namely loop diuretics (eg, furosemide , torsemide , bumetanide ) in either oral or intravenous form.

source_label: Merck Manual, Syncope: if the ECG is unclear, consider a Holter monitor; electrophysiologic testing is used when an abnormality is detected or strongly suspected.
source_quote: Electrophysiologic testing if abnormalities detected or strongly suspected

source_label: Merck Manual, DNR orders: if the patient cannot decide about CPR, a surrogate decides from previously expressed preferences.
source_quote: If the patient is incapable of making a decision about CPR, a surrogate may make the decision based on the patient’s previously expressed preferences

source_label: ACOG, Mammography and other screening tests: average-risk screening mammography is recommended every 1 to 2 years beginning at age 40.
source_quote: If you are at average risk of breast cancer, screening mammography is recommended every 1 to 2 years beginning at age 40.

source_label: Merck Manual, acute diabetes complications: hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state is severe hyperglycemia and hyperosmolality without significant ketosis.
source_quote: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state is diagnosed by severe hyperglycemia and plasma hyperosmolality in the absence of significant ketosis.

source_label: Merck Manual, Hypertension: stage 2 hypertension is treated with an ACE inhibitor or ARB plus a diuretic or a calcium-channel blocker.
source_quote: Adults with stage 2 hypertension (systolic BP ≥ 140/diastolic BP ≥ 90 mm Hg) should be treated initially with 2 first line medications: an ACE inhibitor or ARB combined with either a diuretic or a calcium channel blocker.

source_label: Merck Manual, Blood Products: four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate is the first choice for urgent warfarin reversal.
source_quote: FFP is used for urgent warfarin reversal only when a 4 factor- prothrombin complex concentrate (4F-PCC is the first choice) is unavailable.

source_label: Merck Manual, Angioedema: ACE-inhibitor angioedema usually resolves within 24 to 48 hours after the drug is stopped.
source_quote: Angioedema due to ACE inhibitor use usually resolves about 24 to 48 hours after stopping the medication.

source_label: Merck Manual, Community-acquired pneumonia: clinical severity determines inpatient versus outpatient treatment, and treatment is empiric antibiotics.
source_quote: In general, the clinical severity (ie, risk stratification) of the pneumonia determines the treatment setting (ie, outpatient versus inpatient).

source_label: Merck Manual, Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia: phototherapy thresholds for infants born at 35 weeks or later depend on gestational age and neurotoxicity risk factors.
source_quote: For neonates born at ≥ 35 weeks gestation, there are gestational age-specific phototherapy guidelines.

source_label: Merck Manual, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (polycystic ovary syndrome): adolescents need both a persistent abnormal bleeding pattern and hyperandrogenism.
source_quote: These criteria require that both of the following conditions be present: Abnormal uterine bleeding pattern (abnormal for age or gynecologic age [age minus age at menarche] or symptoms that persist for 1 to 2 years) Evidence of hyperandrogenism (persistently elevated serum testosterone levels above adult norms, moderate to severe hirsutism, or moderate to severe inflammatory acne vulgaris)

source_label: Merck Manual, Hip Fractures: a displaced fracture leaves the leg shortened and externally rotated, and the patient cannot walk.
source_quote: Patients with displaced fractures cannot walk and have significant pain; the affected leg may appear shortened and externally rotated.
